text:
RESOLVED AGAINST ME. sqrt(M+1) is correct. My question was based on a faulty derivation and I am closing this bead as invalid.

I said this was settleable exactly without Monte Carlo on the package, and that whoever owns evidence-sampling-v1 was better placed to do it. That was an unnecessary hand-off - the estimator algebra is small enough to simulate directly at high precision with no package involved, which is what I should have done before filing. 20000 replicates per cell, P = 200, delta_m = mu + eps_m with eps_m iid N(0, xi I_P), edge estimates t(delta_m) %*% delta_n / P, all-pairs mean, naive SE = sd(edges)/sqrt(N):

SIGNAL-DOMINATED REGIME (true distance large relative to the noise term):

  M      true SD    mean naive     ratio    sqrt(M-1)   sqrt(M+1)
  3      0.41049      0.18576     2.2097      1.4142      2.0000
  4      0.35575      0.14839     2.3975      1.7321      2.2361
  6      0.28980      0.10544     2.7484      2.2361      2.6458
  8      0.25171      0.08145     3.0903      2.6458      3.0000
  12     0.20334      0.05595     3.6343      3.3166      3.6056
  20     0.15776      0.03449     4.5745      4.3589      4.5826

  residual vs sqrt(M+1)   +0.21 +0.16 +0.10 +0.09 +0.03 -0.008    CONVERGING TO ZERO
  residual vs sqrt(M-1)   +0.80 +0.67 +0.51 +0.44 +0.32 +0.22     NOT CONVERGING

At M = 20 the ratio is within 0.2 percent of sqrt(M+1) and 4.7 percent from sqrt(M-1). The contract constant is right.

NULL REGIME, for contrast: the ratio goes to 1 as M grows - 1.137, 1.058, 1.018, 1.013, 0.999 at M = 3,4,6,8,12 - confirming that the naive across-edges SE is correct under the null and wrong only when a real effect is present. That matches everything found earlier.

WHERE THE ERROR CAME FROM, because it is instructive. The empirical figures I cited when filing this bead - 1.92, 2.05, 2.41, 2.73, 3.25 - came from a simulation at a moderate effect size that was NOT fully signal-dominated. In that regime the ratio sits between 1, the null limit, and sqrt(M+1), the signal-dominated limit. Those mid-regime numbers happen to pass near sqrt(M-1) around M = 12, and that coincidence was extrapolated into an asymptote it does not have.

So the ratio interpolates between 1 and sqrt(M+1) as effect size grows. sqrt(M-1) is not a limit of anything; it was a curve fitted to points from the wrong regime and then justified after the fact by a reading of Eq. 35.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, precisely:
  the constant                     sqrt(M-1) is not the asymptote; sqrt(M+1) is
  the reading of Eq. 35            attributing 1/(M(M-1)) scaling to the naive SE throughout
                                   was the specific error - it does not scale that way once the
                                   signal term dominates
  the direction of approach        I noted earlier that the curve approaches from above rather
                                   than below, and treated that as a detail. It was the symptom.
                                   A curve approaching a putative asymptote from the wrong side
                                   and never crossing cleanly is evidence the asymptote is wrong.

TO THE CONTRACT OWNER: your constant stands, no change needed, and I withdraw the question. I should have run twelve lines of algebra before asking you to check your own work.
